heading: Reform, don’t target
author: GenZeditor in Gen Zedits /  Sep 21, 2026, 21:40 IST
paragraphs: They took many years to build their strong reputation
Since the 1990s, companies and universities around the world have hired more IIT graduates
Their success is not only because some students get very high salaries

It is also because IITs train students through difficult entrance exams, excellent teachers, strong links with industry and a deep focus on science, maths and engineering.But IITs are also facing a serious problem
Several students at IIT Bombay and IIT Delhi have died by suicide in recent years
Students may face pressure from exams, failure, discrimination, loneliness or depression
Their problems must be taken seriously, and they should receive counselling and support.At the same time, people should not blame teachers or college leaders without knowing all the facts
IITs must maintain high academic standards, but they must also help students who are struggling.One major problem is the shortage of teachers
The number of students in India’s 23 IITs has doubled in about ten years, but the number of teachers has not increased enough
More teachers are needed so that students can get proper guidance and support
IITs already have committees and complaint systems, but these systems must work better
The institutions should listen to students, teachers and alumni, and make meaningful reforms.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.
